manner.en: captured then killed implied by campaign

sourceDate.text: with Wu Fan, Liu Dun, Zhao Da circle

value.statement: still young / a child at father's death

units.zh: 吳范字文則，會稽上虞人也。
units.en: Wu Fan, whose courtesy name was Wenze, came from Shangyu in Kuaiji Commandery.
units.literal: Wu Fan, courtesy name Wenze, was a man of Shangyu in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 以治歷數知風氣聞於郡中。
units.en: He earned local renown for calendar science, numerology, and interpreting weather signs.
units.literal: He became known in the commandery for mastering calendars and reckoning and reading winds and qi.

units.zh: 舉有道，詣京都，世亂不行。
units.en: Recommended for the “Abundant in the Way” candidacy and called to the capital, he stayed home because the realm was in chaos.
units.literal: Recommended as Abundant in the Way, he was summoned to the capital, but with the age in turmoil he did not go.

units.zh: 會孫權起於東南，范委身服事，每有災祥，輒推數言狀。
units.en: After Sun Quan rose in the southeast Wu Fan entered his service—whenever heaven sent prodigies he cast figures and explained what they meant.
units.literal: When Sun Quan arose in the southeast Fan devoted himself to service; whenever omens of fortune or disaster appeared he always reckoned by numbers and stated their forms.

units.zh: 其術多效，遂以顯名。
units.en: Again and again his calculations held, and his name spread.
units.literal: His arts proved effective many times, and so he became famous.

units.zh: 初，權在吳，欲討黃祖。
units.en: Early on, while Sun Quan held Wu and planned to attack Huang Zu,
units.literal: At first, when Quan was at Wu and wished to campaign against Huang Zu,

units.zh: 范曰：“今茲少利，不如明年。
units.en: Wu Fan said, “Victory this round would be small—wait until next year.
units.literal: Fan said: “This year brings slight gain—it is not as good as next year.

units.zh: 明年戊子，荊州劉表亦身死國亡。”
units.en: Next year falls under wuzi—Liu Biao of Jingzhou will die and his domain collapse.”
units.literal: Next year is wuzi; in Jingzhou Liu Biao too will die and his state perish.”

units.zh: 權遂征祖，卒不能克。
units.en: Sun Quan attacked anyway and failed to break Huang Zu.
units.literal: Quan then campaigned against Zu but could not overcome him.

units.zh: 明年，軍出，行及尋陽，范見風氣，因詣船賀，催兵急行，至即破祖，祖得夜亡。
units.en: The following year the fleet advanced; at Xunyang Wu Fan read the omens, boarded Sun Quan’s ship to offer congratulations, and pressed for speed—they smashed Huang Zu, who fled under cover of night.
units.literal: The next year the army set out; reaching Xunyang Fan observed the qi, boarded a ship to congratulate Quan, and urged the troops to march hard—on arrival they broke Zu; Zu fled by night.

units.zh: 權恐失之，范曰：“未遠，必生禽祖。”
units.en: Sun Quan feared losing the prey; Wu Fan said, “Huang Zu cannot have gone far—you will take him alive.”
units.literal: Quan feared losing him; Fan said: “He has not gone far—you will surely capture Zu alive.”

units.zh: 至五更中，果得之。
units.en: Before dawn broke they had him in hand.
units.literal: By the fifth watch they indeed seized him.

units.zh: 劉表竟死，荊州分割。
units.en: Liu Biao died on schedule and Jingzhou was partitioned.
units.literal: Liu Biao died as predicted and Jingzhou was carved up.

units.zh: 及壬辰歲，范又白言：“歲在甲午，劉備當得益州。”
units.en: In the renchen year Wu Fan added: “When the cycle reaches jiawu, Liu Bei will win Yizhou.”
units.literal: In the renchen year Fan again reported: “When the year reaches jiawu, Liu Bei will obtain Yizhou.”

units.zh: 後呂岱從蜀還，遇之白帝，說備部眾離落，死亡且半，事必不克。
units.en: Later Lü Dai came back from Shu and told Sun Quan at Baidi that Liu Bei’s army was shattered and half gone—the conquest would fail.
units.literal: Later Lü Dai returned from Shu and met Quan at Baidi, reporting that Bei’s troops were scattered and half dead—the affair could not succeed.

units.zh: 權以難范，范曰：“臣所言者天道也，而岱所見者人事耳。”
units.en: Sun Quan challenged him with Lü Dai’s report; Wu Fan replied, “I speak heaven’s pattern—Lü Dai saw only human circumstance.”
units.literal: Quan pressed Fan with this difficulty; Fan said: “What your servant speaks is Heaven’s way—what Dai saw is merely human affairs.”

units.zh: 備卒得蜀。
units.en: Liu Bei took Shu just as predicted.
units.literal: Bei ultimately obtained Shu.

units.zh: 權與呂蒙謀襲關羽，議之近臣，多曰不可。
units.en: Sun Quan and Lü Meng planned to ambush Guan Yu; most of his inner circle said no.
units.literal: Quan plotted with Lü Meng to surprise Guan Yu; consulting close ministers, most said it could not be done.

units.zh: 權以問範，範曰：“得之。”
units.en: Sun Quan asked Wu Fan; Fan said, “You will take him.”
units.literal: Quan asked Fan; Fan said: “You will obtain him.”

units.zh: 後羽在麥城，使使請降。
units.en: Later Guan Yu holed up in Wheat Castle and offered submission.
units.literal: Later Yu was at Wheat Castle and sent envoys seeking surrender.

units.zh: 權問范曰：“競當降否？”
units.en: Sun Quan pressed, “Is the surrender genuine?”
units.literal: Quan asked Fan: “Will he truly surrender?”

units.zh: 范曰：“彼有走氣，言降詐話耳。”
units.en: Wu Fan answered, “His aura shows flight—the surrender talk is a lie.”
units.literal: Fan said: “He has the qi of flight—talk of surrender is deceit.”

units.zh: 權使潘璋邀其徑路，覘候者還，自羽已去。
units.en: Sun Quan sent Pan Zhang to cut his retreat; scouts reported Guan Yu had slipped away.
units.literal: Quan dispatched Pan Zhang to block his route; scouts returned reporting Yu had already gone.

units.zh: 范曰：“雖去不免。”
units.en: Wu Fan insisted, “Even gone he cannot escape.”
units.literal: Fan said: “Though he has gone he will not escape.”

units.zh: 問其期，曰：“明日日中。”
units.en: Asked when, he said, “Tomorrow at midday.”
units.literal: Asked the date, he said: “Tomorrow at noon.”

units.zh: 權立表下漏以待之。
units.en: Sun Quan set a water-clock under a sundial and waited.
units.literal: Quan set a clepsydra beneath a gnomon and waited.

units.zh: 及中不至，權問其故，范曰：“時尚未正中也。”
units.en: Midday came and went; Sun Quan demanded why—Wu Fan said, “True solar noon has not arrived.”
units.literal: When noon passed without event Quan asked the reason; Fan said: “The moment is not yet true noon.”

units.zh: 頃之，有風動帷，范拊手曰：“羽至矣。”
units.en: Soon a breeze rattled the drapes; Wu Fan cried, “Guan Yu is here.”
units.literal: Presently wind stirred the curtains; Fan clapped his hands and said: “Yu has arrived.”

units.zh: 須臾，外稱萬歲，傳言得羽。
units.en: Moments later cheers rang outside—Guan Yu had been captured.
units.literal: Shortly voices outside shouted “Long live!”—word came that Yu had been taken.

units.zh: 後權與魏為好，范曰：“以風氣言之，彼以貌來，其實有謀，宜為之備。”
units.en: When Sun Quan befriended Wei, Wu Fan warned, “Their winds bear smiles yet hide knives—brace yourself.”
units.literal: Later Quan made peace with Wei; Fan said: “Judging by qi they come with friendly faces but harbor plots—you should prepare.

units.zh: 劉備盛兵西陵，范曰：“後當和親。”
units.en: When Liu Bei stacked armies at Xiling, Wu Fan said, “Peace through marriage will follow.”
units.literal: Liu Bei massed troops at Xiling; Fan said: “Later there will be marriage alliance.”

units.zh: 終皆如言。
units.en: Every prediction landed.
units.literal: All ended as he spoke.

units.zh: 其占驗明審如此。
units.en: His forecasts proved this precise.
units.literal: His divinations were this clear and exact.

units.zh: 權以范為騎都尉，領太史令，數從訪問，欲知其決。
units.en: Sun Quan named him Colonel of Cavalry and Superintendent of Astrology, questioning him often and pressing for his inner formulas.
units.literal: Quan appointed Fan Colonel of Cavalry and concurrent Grand Clerk of Astrology, repeatedly consulting him and wishing to know his decisive methods.

units.zh: 范秘惜其術，不以至要語權。
units.en: Wu Fan hoarded his secrets and never revealed the core techniques.
units.literal: Fan closely guarded his arts and did not tell Quan the essentials.

units.zh: 權由是恨之。
units.en: Sun Quan grew to resent him.
units.literal: Thereupon Quan resented him.

units.zh: 〈《吴录》曰：范独心计，所以见重者术，术亡则身弃矣，故终不言。〉
units.en: 〈The Record of Wu notes Wu Fan hoarded his craft because patrons valued only the magic—lose that and they discard you—so he stayed silent.〉
units.literal: 〈The Wu lu says: Fan relied on solitary calculation—what won esteem was the art; once the art vanished the body would be cast aside—hence he never spoke.〉

units.zh: 初，權為將軍時，范嘗白言“江南有王氣，亥子之間有大福慶。”
units.en: While Sun Quan still held the rank of general Wu Fan once said, “South of the river carries imperial vapors—between the hai and zi hours supreme fortune awaits.”
units.literal: At first, when Quan was General, Fan once reported: “South of the Yangzi bears kingly qi; between hai and zi great blessing will come.”

units.zh: 權曰：“若終如言，以君為候。”
units.en: Sun Quan replied, “If it comes true I will make you a marquis.”
units.literal: Quan said: “If it ends as you say I shall enfeoff you as marquis.”

units.zh: 及立為吳王，范時侍宴。
units.en: When Sun Quan became King of Wu, Wu Fan waited on him at a feast.
units.literal: When he was invested King of Wu Fan attended a banquet.

units.zh: 曰：“昔在吳中，嘗言此事，大王識之邪？”
units.en: He asked, “Do you recall what I said back in Wu?”
units.literal: He said: “Back in Wu I spoke of this—does Your Majesty remember?”

units.zh: 權曰：“有之。”
units.en: Sun Quan answered, “I remember.”
units.literal: Quan said: “It is so.”

units.zh: 因呼左右，以侯綬帶范。
units.en: He ordered servants to present the marquis cords.
units.literal: He called attendants to bring Fan a marquis’s ribbon.

units.zh: 范權知權欲以厭當前言，輒手推不受。
units.en: Wu Fan saw Sun Quan meant only to paper over an old promise and thrust the cords back untouched.
units.literal: Fan knew Quan wished to satisfy the earlier words with a gesture and pushed the gift away, refusing to accept.

units.zh: 及後論功行封，以范為都亭侯，詔臨當出，權恚其愛道於己也，削除其名。
units.en: When rewards were handed out Wu Fan received a village marquisate; just before the edict Sun Quan, enraged that Wu Fan prized arcana above loyalty to him, erased his name.
units.literal: Later when merits were weighed for enfeoffment Fan was named Village Marquis; as the edict was about to issue Quan, furious that Fan loved his Dao more than himself, struck his name off.

units.zh: 范為人剛直，頗好自稱，然與親故交接有終始。
units.en: Wu Fan was rigid and self-promoting, yet friendships with intimates lasted lifelong.
units.literal: Fan was blunt by nature and inclined to boast, yet with kin and old friends his dealings had constancy from start to finish.

units.zh: 素與魏滕同邑相善。
units.en: He had long been close to Wei Teng from his home county.
units.literal: From youth he was on good terms with Wei Teng of the same district.

units.zh: 滕嘗有罪，權責怒甚嚴，敢有諫者死，范謂滕曰：“與汝偕死。”
units.en: Wei Teng once broke the law; Sun Quan’s rage terrified the court—death awaited any advisor—Wu Fan told him, “I perish at your side.”
units.literal: Teng once offended the law; Quan’s wrath was fierce—whoever remonstrated would die; Fan told Teng: “I die with you.”

units.zh: 滕曰：“死而無益，何用死為？”
units.en: Wei Teng answered, “Useless death helps nothing.”
units.literal: Teng said: “Death without profit—what use is dying?”

units.zh: 范曰：“安能慮此坐觀汝邪？”
units.en: Wu Fan shot back, “Could I sit idle while you hang?”
units.literal: Fan said: “How could I sit watching you?”

units.zh: 乃髡頭自縛詣門下，使鈴下以聞。
units.en: He shaved his head, tied his own bonds, and appeared at the palace gate, telling the usher to announce him.
units.literal: Thereupon he shaved his head, bound himself, and presented himself at the gate, ordering the bell-man to announce him.

units.zh: 鈴下不敢，曰：“必死，不敢白。”
units.en: The usher refused: “Reporting means death—I cannot.”
units.literal: The bell-man dared not, saying: “Certain death—I dare not report.”

units.zh: 范曰：“汝有子邪？”
units.en: Wu Fan asked, “Do you have children?”
units.literal: Fan said: “Do you have a son?”

units.en: “I do.”
units.literal: He said: “Yes.”

units.zh: 曰：“使汝為吳范死，子以屬我。”
units.en: Wu Fan said, “Die for me and I will raise your boy.”
units.literal: Fan said: “If you die for Wu Fan I entrust your son to me.”

units.zh: 鈴下曰：“諾。”
units.en: The usher said, “Done.”
units.literal: The bell-man said: “Agreed.”

units.zh: 乃排閤入。
units.en: He burst through the gate.
units.literal: He pushed through the gate.

units.zh: 言未卒，權大怒，欲便投以戟。
units.en: Sun Quan roared mid-sentence and reached for a halberd.
units.literal: Before the words finished Quan was furious and wished at once to hurl a halberd at him.

units.zh: 逡巡走出，范因突入，叩頭流血，言與涕並。
units.en: Attendants wavered and withdrew; Wu Fan darted in, beating his brow bloody, words lost in sobs.
units.literal: Hesitating he walked out; Fan then rushed in, knocking his head until it bled, speech and tears mingling.

units.zh: 良久，權意釋，乃免滕。
units.en: After a long while Sun Quan's anger eased, and he spared Wei Teng.
units.literal: After a long while Quan's anger eased, and he spared Teng.

units.zh: 滕見范謝曰：“父母能生長我，不能免我於死。
units.en: Wei Teng thanked Wu Fan, saying, “Parents give life but cannot spare me from execution.
units.literal: Teng thanked Fan, saying: “Parents bear and rear me yet cannot save me from death.

units.zh: 丈夫相知，如汝足矣，何用多為！”
units.en: A friend like you satisfies a man—what more could I want?”
units.literal: To know a man as you do contents a husband—what need of more!”

units.zh: 〈《会稽典录》曰：滕字周林，祖父河内太守朗，字少英，列在八俊。
units.en: 〈The Kuaiji Canon records: Wei Teng, courtesy name Zhoulin—his grandfather Lang, courtesy name Shaoying, was Administrator of Henei and ranked among the Eight Talents.
units.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu says: Teng, courtesy name Zhoulin—his grandfather Lang was Administrator of Henei, courtesy name Shaoying, numbered among the Eight Heroes.

units.zh: 滕性刚直，行不苟合，虽遭困偪，终不回挠。
units.en: Wei Teng was stubborn and principled; hardship never broke him.
units.literal: Teng’s nature was blunt; his conduct admitted no compromise; though pressed by hardship he never bent.

units.zh: 初亦迕策，几殆，赖太妃救得免，语见《妃嫔传》。
units.en: He once defied Sun Ce and nearly died—Lady Wu saved him; see the concubine chapter.
units.literal: At first he also crossed Ce and nearly perished—only the Senior Concubine’s rescue spared him; the tale appears in the Biographies of Imperial Concubines.

units.zh: 历阳、鄱阳、山阴三县令，鄱阳太守。〉
units.en: He served as magistrate of Liyang, Poyang, and Shanyin, then as Administrator of Poyang.〉
units.literal: Magistrate of three counties—Liyang, Poyang, and Shanyin—and Administrator of Poyang—end of gloss.〉

units.zh: 黃武五年，范病卒。
units.en: Huangwu 5 Wu Fan died of illness.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Huangwu Fan died of illness.

units.zh: 長子先死，少子尚幼，於是業絕。
units.en: His firstborn had died; the youngest was a child—his lineage of arts died with him.
units.literal: His eldest son had predeceased him; the youngest was still a boy—thus his teaching ended.

units.zh: 權追思之，募三州有能舉知術數如吳范、趙達者，封千戶侯，卒無所得。
units.en: Sun Quan mourned him and promised a thousand-household marquisate to anyone who matched Wu Fan or Zhao Da’s skill—no one qualified.
units.literal: Quan remembered him and offered across three provinces a thousand-household marquisate to whoever could match Wu Fan or Zhao Da in numerology—none was found.

units.zh: 〈《吴录》曰：范先知其死日，谓权曰：“陛下某日当丧军师。”
units.en: 〈The Record of Wu adds: Wu Fan predicted his death and told Sun Quan, “You will lose your strategist on a set day.”
units.literal: 〈The Wu lu says: Fan knew beforehand his death-day and told Quan: “Your Majesty will lose your army counselor on such-and-such a day.”

units.zh: 权曰：“吾无军师，焉得丧之？”
units.en: Sun Quan replied, “I employ no strategist—what loss is there?”
units.literal: Quan said: “I have no army counselor—how can I lose him?”

units.zh: 范曰：“陛下出军临敌，须臣言而后行，臣乃陛下之军师也。”
units.en: Wu Fan answered, “When you march you wait on my counsel—I am your strategist.”
units.literal: Fan said: “Whenever Your Majesty campaigns you await my word—your servant is Your Majesty’s strategist.”

units.zh: 至其日果卒。
units.en: He died exactly then.
units.literal: On that day he indeed died.

units.zh: 臣松之案，范死时，权未称帝，此云陛下，非也。〉
units.en: Pei Songzhi observes Sun Quan was not yet emperor when Wu Fan died—“Your Majesty” is anachronistic.〉
units.literal: Pei Songzhi notes: When Fan died Quan had not yet taken the imperial title—the word “Your Majesty” here is incorrect.〉

units.zh: 劉惇字子仁，平原人也。
units.en: Liu Dun, courtesy Ziren, hailed from Pingyuan.
units.literal: Liu Dun, courtesy name Ziren, was a man of Pingyuan.

units.zh: 遭亂避地，客游廬陵，事孫輔。
units.en: He escaped chaos, lodged in Luling, and served Sun Fu.
units.literal: He fled turmoil and wandered to Luling as a guest, serving Sun Fu.

units.zh: 以明天官達占數顯於南土。
units.en: Southern patrons esteemed him for astrology and divination math.
units.literal: He became eminent in the south through mastery of celestial offices and prognostic reckoning.

units.zh: 每有水旱寇賊，皆先時處期，無不中者。
units.en: Floods, droughts, raids—he dated each before it arrived.
units.literal: Whenever flood, drought, or banditry struck he foretold the season beforehand—never missed.

units.zh: 輔異焉，以為軍師，軍中鹹敬事之，號曰神明。
units.en: Sun Fu named him strategist; the camp hailed him as a spirit.
units.literal: Fu marveled and appointed him army strategist; the entire army revered him and called him divine.

units.zh: 建安中，孫權在豫章，時有星變，以問惇。
units.en: In Jian’an Sun Quan camped at Yuzhang; strange stars appeared and he consulted Liu Dun.
units.literal: During the Jian’an era Sun Quan was at Yuzhang when stellar anomalies appeared—he questioned Dun.

units.zh: 惇曰："災在丹楊。
units.en: Liu Dun said, “Calamity will strike Danyang.”
units.literal: Dun said: “Disaster lies in Danyang.”

units.zh: "權曰："何如？
units.en: Sun Quan asked, “What form will it take?”
units.literal: Quan said: “How so?”

units.zh: "曰："客勝主人，到某日當得問。
units.en: He answered, “The outsider bests the insider—you will hear by a set date.”
units.literal: He said: “The guest conquers the master—by such-and-such a day news will arrive.”

units.zh: "是時邊鴻作亂，卒如惇言。
units.en: Then Bian Hong rose in revolt—exactly as Liu Dun foretold.
units.literal: At that time Bian Hong rebelled—it ended as Dun predicted.

units.zh: 惇於諸術皆善，尤明太一，皆能推演其事，窮盡要妙，著書百餘篇，名儒刁玄稱以為奇。
units.en: Liu Dun mastered many disciplines, especially Taiyi divination, unfolding cases to their subtle roots in over a hundred scrolls—scholar Diao Xuan called them extraordinary.
units.literal: Dun excelled in every art and especially understood the Taiyi method—he could unfold events from it to exhaust subtle essentials; he wrote more than a hundred chapters; the eminent scholar Diao Xuan praised them as marvelous.

units.zh: 惇亦寶愛其術，不以告人，故世莫得而明也。
units.en: Yet Liu Dun hoarded his secrets, so posterity never fully grasped them.
units.literal: Dun also treasured his arts and told no one—hence the age could not understand them clearly.

units.zh: 趙達，河南人也。
units.en: Zhao Da came from Henan.
units.literal: Zhao Da was a man of Henan.

units.zh: 少從漢侍中單甫受學，用思精密。
units.en: Youth brought tutelage under Han Attendant Shan Fu; his reasoning ran fine-toothed.
units.literal: In youth he studied under Palace Attendant Shan Fu of Han, thinking with exquisite precision.

units.zh: 謂東南有王者氣，可以避難，故脫身渡江。
units.en: He read kingly qi in the southeast and crossed the river to escape turmoil.
units.literal: He said the southeast bore an aura of kingship where one might flee disaster—therefore he crossed the Yangzi.

units.zh: 治九宮一算之術，究其微旨，是以能應機立成。
units.en: He perfected nine-palace calculation, grasped its marrow, and answered riddles instantly.
units.literal: He cultivated the nine-palace reckoning art, plumbing its subtle intent—thus he could answer on the spot.

units.zh: 對問若神，至計飛蝗，射隱伏，無不中效。
units.en: Whether counting flying locusts mid-flight or guessing concealed totals, he never missed.
units.literal: His replies seemed supernatural—reckoning flying locusts or shooting hidden quantities—never failing.

units.zh: 或難達曰：飛者固不可校，誰知其然，此殆妄耳。
units.en: Skeptics said airborne swarms cannot be tallied—his claims had to be fraud.
units.literal: Someone challenged Da: flying things cannot be counted—who knows it true—this must be nonsense.”

units.zh: "達使其人取小豆數鬥，播之席上，立處其數，驗覆果信。
units.en: Zhao Da poured beans across a mat, announced the total at once, and a recount proved him right.
units.literal: Da had the man take several pecks of beans, scatter them on a mat, instantly stated the count, and verification by recount proved true.

units.zh: 嘗過知故，知故為之具食。
units.en: Once he dropped on an old friend who laid out a meal.
units.literal: He once visited an old acquaintance who prepared food for him.

units.zh: 食畢，謂曰："倉卒乏酒，又無佳看，無以敘意，如何?"達因取盤中只箸，再三從橫之，乃言："卿東壁下有美酒一斛，又有鹿肉三斤，何以辭無?"時坐有他賓，內得主人情。
units.en: After the meal the host said they suddenly lacked wine and fine dishes with which to show goodwill—Zhao Da then took the single chopsticks from the dish, crossed them repeatedly, and declared that east of the east wall lay a hu of fine wine and three jin of venison; other guests present inwardly grasped the host's embarrassment.
units.literal: When they finished eating he said: “Suddenly we lack wine and fine dishes—nothing to express good will—what can we do?” Da took the single chopsticks from the dish, crossed them again and again, then said: “East of your east wall lies a hu of fine wine and three jin of venison—why claim you have nothing?” Other guests were present and inwardly grasped the host’s embarrassment.

units.zh: 主有慚曰："以卿善射有無，欲相試耳，竟效如此。
units.en: The host admitted embarrassment: “I meant only to test your gift for sensing what was hidden—it worked exactly as you claimed.”
units.literal: The host said ashamedly: “Because you excel at telling whether things exist or not I wished to try you—yet it came out thus.”

units.zh: "遂出酒酣飲。
units.en: They broke out the wine and drank freely.
units.literal: Thereupon he produced wine and they drank deep.

units.zh: 又有書簡上作千萬數，著空倉中封之，令達算之。
units.en: Another test wrote a huge figure on a slip, locked it in an empty granary, and told Zhao Da to divine the number.
units.literal: Again someone wrote a sum to ten millions on paper, sealed it inside an empty granary, and ordered Da to reckon it.

units.zh: 達處如數，云："但有名無實。
units.en: Zhao Da named the total and added, “The tally exists on paper—the granary stays empty.”
units.literal: Da stated the figure correctly and said: “There is only the reputation—no substance.”

units.zh: "其精微若是。
units.en: His precision ran that deep.
units.literal: His subtle craft reached such refinement.

units.zh: 達寶惜其術，自闞澤、殷禮皆名儒善士，親屈節就學，達秘而不告，太史丞公孫滕少師事達，勤勞累年，達許教之者有年數矣，臨當喻語而輒復止。
units.en: Zhao Da hoarded his methods: Kan Ze and Yin Li came as humble pupils yet learned nothing; Gongsun Teng toiled years as his disciple—each time Zhao Da neared disclosure he pulled back.
units.literal: Da treasured his arts—even Kan Ze and Yin Li, eminent scholars and upright men, humbled themselves to learn from him, yet Da kept silence and would not instruct them; Assistant Clerk of Astrology Gongsun Teng studied as his disciple from youth and labored many years—Da for several years promised to teach him, yet whenever about to explain he broke off again.

units.zh: 滕他日□酒具，侯顏色，拜跪而請。
units.en: Another day Gongsun Teng laid out food and wine, read Zhao Da’s temper, and begged on his knees.
units.literal: Another day Teng prepared wine and fare, watched Da’s mood, knelt and pleaded.

units.zh: 達曰："吾先人得此術，欲圖為帝王師，至仕來三世，不過太史郎，誠不欲復傳之。
units.en: Zhao Da answered, “Our ancestors meant this lore for dynastic tutors—three generations stalled at petty astrology posts—I hate passing it down.”
units.literal: Da said: “My forebears gained this art hoping to instruct emperors—yet three generations of office never rose past Clerk Astrologer—I truly shrink from handing it on.

units.zh: 且此術微妙，頭乘尾除，一算之法，父子不相語。
units.en: The method is delicate—operations compound and reduce—and families guard even one formula from kin.
units.literal: Moreover the craft is subtle—multiply at the head, divide at the tail—one reckoning path—fathers and sons do not speak it between themselves.

units.zh: 然以子篤好不倦，今真以相授矣。
units.en: Because you never slackened in zeal, I will actually teach you.
units.literal: Yet because you love it earnestly without tiring, now I truly entrust it to you.”

units.zh: "飲酒數行，達起取素書兩眷，大如手指，達曰："當寫讀此，由自解也。
units.en: He rose after a few cups and produced two finger-sized booklets: “Copy these out—understanding will follow.”
units.literal: After several rounds of drinking Da rose and fetched two plain scrolls each the width of a finger; Da said: “Write them out and read—you will grasp them yourself.

units.zh: 吾久廢，不復省之。
units.en: He claimed he had neglected the texts and barely remembered them.
units.literal: I have neglected them long—I no longer review them.

units.zh: 今欲思論一過，數日當以相與。
units.en: He asked for days to review before handing them over.
units.literal: Now I wish to think through them once—in a few days I shall give them to you.”

units.zh: "滕如期往，至乃陽求索書，驚言失之，云："女婿昨來，必是渠所竊。
units.en: When Gongsun Teng returned, Zhao Da feigned panic—the manuals were gone—blaming the son-in-law.
units.literal: Teng arrived on time; Da pretended to hunt for the books and cried that they were lost, saying: “My son-in-law visited yesterday—he must have stolen them.”

units.zh: "遂從此絕。
units.en: The lessons ended there.
units.literal: From this the instruction ceased.

units.zh: 初，孫權行師征伐，每令達有所推步，皆如其言。
units.en: Whenever Sun Quan marched he made Zhao Da cast ahead—and each forecast hit.
units.literal: At first when Sun Quan campaigned he always ordered Da to forecast events—they always matched his words.

units.zh: 權問其法，達終不語，由此見薄，祿位不至。
units.en: Sun Quan demanded the technique; Zhao Da stayed mute—so courtiers snubbed him and promotions stopped.
units.literal: Quan asked his method—Da never spoke—therefore he was slighted and salary and rank never rose.

units.zh: 〈吴书曰：初，权即尊号，令达算作天子之后，当复几年？
units.en: 〈The Book of Wu adds that after Sun Quan took the throne he asked Zhao Da how long his mandate would run.
units.literal: 〈The Wu shu says: When Quan first assumed the imperial title he ordered Da to reckon how many years remained under Heaven after the Son of Heaven—how many years until repetition?

units.zh: 达曰：“高祖建元十二年，陛下倍之。”
units.en: Zhao Da answered, “Gaozu's reign-era ran twelve years—Your Majesty will double that.”
units.literal: Da said: “Gaozu founded his reign-name in the twelfth year—Your Majesty doubles it.”

units.zh: 权大喜，左右称万岁。
units.en: Sun Quan cheered; the hall cried long life.
units.literal: Quan rejoiced greatly; attendants shouted “Ten thousand years!”

units.zh: 果如达言。〉
units.en: Events matched Zhao Da’s reckoning.〉
units.literal: It indeed happened as Da said.〉

units.zh: 達常笑謂諸星氣風術者曰："當回算帷幕，不出戶牖以知天道，而反晝夜暴露以望氣樣，不亦難乎!"閒居無為，引算自校，乃歎曰："吾算訖盡某年月日，其終矣。
units.en: Zhao Da mocked outdoor astrologers—true skill needed no sky-gazing—then computed his own death date and sighed it aloud.
units.literal: Da often laughed at star-and-wind diviners: “You ought to reckon behind curtain and screen, know Heaven’s way without leaving doors and windows—yet you expose yourselves day and night watching qi—is it not painful!” Dwelling idle he pushed tallies and checked himself, then sighed: “My reckoning exhausts itself on such year month day—that is my end.

units.zh: "達妻數見達效，聞而哭泣。
units.en: His wife had seen his arts work—she wept at the sentence.
units.literal: Da’s wife had often witnessed Da’s efficacy—hearing this she wept.

units.zh: 達欲弭妻意，乃更步算，言："向者謬誤耳，尚未也。
units.en: To calm her he recast the figures: “I miscalculated—the hour has not come.”
units.literal: Da wished to soothe his wife—he paced calculations again and said: “Earlier I erred—not yet.”

units.zh: "後如期死。
units.en: He died exactly when first predicted.
units.literal: Later he died on that date.

units.zh: 權聞達有書，求之不得，乃錄問其女，及發棺無所得，法術絕焉。
units.en: Sun Quan hunted Zhao Da’s manuscripts—questioned his daughter—opened the tomb—found nothing—the lineage of lore died.
units.literal: Hearing Da had writings Quan sought them without success—then interrogated his daughter—opening the coffin found nothing—the arts were extinguished.

units.zh: 〈吴录曰：皇象字休明，广陵江都人。
units.en: 〈The Record of Wu names calligrapher Huang Xiang (style Xiuming) from Jiangdu.
units.literal: 〈The Wu lu says: Huang Xiang, courtesy Xiuming, was a man of Jiangdu in Guangling.

units.zh: 幼工书。
units.en: He practiced brushwork from boyhood.
units.literal: Skilled in writing from youth.

units.zh: 时有张子并、陈梁甫能书。
units.en: Zhang Zibing and Chen Liangfu were rivals in script.
units.literal: At the time Zhang Zibing and Chen Liangfu could write.

units.zh: 甫恨逋，并恨峻，象斟酌其间，甚得其妙，中国善书者不能及也。
units.en: Huang Xiang balanced their styles and surpassed both—northern masters fell short.
units.literal: Liangfu resented Bu, Zibing resented Jun—Xiang mediated between them and grasped the exquisite point—calligraphers of the Central Plains could not equal him.

units.zh: 严武字子卿，卫尉畯再从子也，围釭莫与为辈。
units.en: Yan Wu (Ziqing), great-grandson of Wei officer Yan Jun, stood alone in bronze-seal carving.
units.literal: Yan Wu, courtesy Ziqing—grand-nephew twice removed of Commandant of the Guards Jun—none matched him in seal-ring engraving.

units.zh: 宋寿占梦，十不失一。
units.en: Song Shuo dream-divined with ninety-percent accuracy.
units.literal: Song Shou interpreted dreams—missed one in ten.

units.zh: 曹不兴善画，权使画屏风，误落笔点素，因就以作蝇。
units.en: Ordered to paint a screen Cao Buxing smeared ink—turned the blot into a fly.
units.literal: Cao Buxing excelled at painting—Quan had him paint a screen—by mistake ink dropped on silk—thereupon he turned it into a fly.

units.zh: 既进御，权以为生蝇，举手弹之。
units.en: Sun Quan tried to swat the painted fly.
units.literal: When presented Quan thought it a living fly and raised his hand to flick it.

units.zh: 孤城郑妪能相人，及范、惇、达八人，世皆称妙，谓之八绝云。
units.en: Physiognomist Mother Zheng of lone-walled Gucheng joined Wu Fan, Liu Dun, Zhao Da, and five talents hailed as the Eight Wonders.
units.literal: Old woman Zheng of Gucheng could read faces—with Fan, Dun, Da and five others the age called them the Eight Marvels.

units.zh: 《晋阳秋曰：吴有葛衡字思真，明达天官，能为几巧，作浑天，使地居于中，以机动之，天转而地止，以上应晷度。〉
units.en: The Jin Yang Qiu credits Ge Heng with a geared cosmos-model matching celestial arcs.〉
units.literal: The Jin Yang Qiu says: Wu had Ge Heng, courtesy Sizhen—understood celestial offices—crafted ingenious devices—made an armillary sphere with earth at the center moved by gears—heaven turned while earth stood still—matching sundial degrees.〉

units.en: Section heading: Appraisal.
units.literal: 【Appraisal】

units.zh: 評曰：三子各於其術精矣，其用思妙矣，然君子等役心神，宜於大者遠者，是以有識之士，捨彼而取此也。
units.en: The historian concludes: technical genius tempts petty wonders; thoughtful men aim higher.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Each of the three men mastered his craft—their application of mind was subtle—yet the gentleman employs spirit on great and distant aims—therefore discerning scholars forsake the former and embrace the latter.

units.zh: 〈孙盛曰：夫玄览未然，逆鉴来事，虽裨灶、梓慎其犹病诸，况术之下此者乎？
units.en: 〈Sun Sheng notes even canonical astrologers stumbled—lesser tricks merit doubt.
units.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: To survey the unseen and mirror coming events—even Pi Zao and Zi Shen struggled—how much more arts beneath theirs?

units.zh: 吴史书达知东南当有王气，故轻举济江。
units.en: Wu records say Zhao Da crossed south chasing imperial vapors.
units.literal: The Wu history says Da knew kingly qi would rise in the southeast—therefore he lightly crossed the Yangzi.

units.zh: 魏承汉绪，受命中畿，达不能豫睹兆萌，而流窜吴越。
units.en: Wei held the Central Plain—yet Zhao Da missed Wei’s rise and wandered eastern marshes.
units.literal: Wei inherited Han’s thread and received mandate in the heartland—Da failed to foresee the budding sign beforehand and drifted among Wu and Yue.

units.zh: 又不知吝术之鄙，见薄於时，安在其能逆睹天道而审帝王之符瑞哉？
units.en: Sun Sheng asks how a stingy technician could read dynastic fate.
units.literal: Again ignorant how base it is to hoard arts—slighted by the age—where lies ability to foresee Heaven’s way and discern imperial portents?

units.zh: 昔圣王观天地之文，以画八卦之象，故亹亹成於蓍策，变化形乎六爻，是以三易虽殊，卦繇理一，安有回转一筹，可以钩深测隐，意对逆占，而能遂知来物者乎？
units.en: The classics unified oracle logic—no single abacus replaces the Changes.
units.literal: Ancient sage kings observed Heaven and Earth’s patterns to fashion the eight trigrams—thus abundant wisdom arose from milfoil and transformation took form in six lines—therefore though three Changes differ hexagram principle is one—how could rotating one tally hook depths and probe concealments or invert divination face-to-face and thereby know future things?

units.zh: 流俗好异，妄设神奇，不幸之中，仲尼所弃，是以君子志其大者，无所取诸。
units.en: Fashion craves miracles—Confucius spurned fortune-telling—the gentleman thinks bigger.
units.literal: Common fashion loves the strange and vainly fabricates marvels—among ill omens Confucius discarded these—therefore the gentleman sets his aim on greatness and takes nothing from such.

units.zh: 臣松之以为盛云“君子志其大者，无所取诸”，故评家之旨，非新声也。
units.en: Pei Songzhi notes Sun Sheng echoes the official appraisal.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: When Sheng says “the gentleman aims at greatness and takes nothing from such”—the appraiser’s meaning is no novelty.

units.zh: 其餘所讥，则皆为非理。
units.en: Pei rejects Sun Sheng’s other barbs.
units.literal: His remaining ridicule is altogether unreasonable.

units.zh: 自中原酷乱，至于建安，数十年间，生民殆尽，比至小康，皆百死之餘耳。
units.en: Decades of northern slaughter left few survivors—peace meant beating overwhelming odds.
units.literal: From central plains cruel chaos until Jian’an—within several decades the living nearly vanished—by modest peace all were survivors of hundred deaths.

units.zh: 江左虽有兵革，不能如中国之甚也，焉知达不算其安危，知祸有多少，利在东南，以全其身乎？
units.en: The south suffered less—Zhao Da may simply have sought safer ground.
units.literal: Though east of the river knew warfare it could not match China’s severity—how know Da did not reckon safety and danger, weigh harm’s measure, and judge profit lay in the southeast to preserve himself?

units.zh: 而责不知魏氏将兴，流播吴越，在京房之筹，犹不能自免刑戮，况达但以秘术见薄，在悔吝之间乎！
units.en: Pinning prophets for politics ignores worse failures—even masters died under suspicion.
units.literal: Yet blame him for not foreknowing Wei’s rise and drifting Wu-Yue—even Jing Fang’s reckonings could not spare execution—how much more Da slighted only for secret arts—between regret and miserliness!

units.zh: 古之道术，盖非一方，探赜之功，岂惟六爻，苟得其要，则可以易而知之矣，回转一筹，胡足怪哉？
units.en: Many roads led to insight—the Changes were broader than one chip.
units.literal: Ancient arts were not one path—work plumbing mysteries used not only six lines—grasp the essentials and you know through Change—rotating one tally—what is strange?

units.zh: 达之推算，穷其要妙以知幽测隐，何愧于古！
units.en: Zhao Da plumbed secrets as well as ancients.
units.literal: Da’s reckonings exhausted subtle essentials to probe depths—what shame before antiquity?

units.zh: 而以裨、梓限之，谓达为妄，非笃论也。
units.en: Equating him with Pi Zao sells Zhao Da short.
units.literal: Yet limiting him with Pi and Zi—calling Da deluded—is not serious judgment.

units.zh: 《抱朴子》曰：时有葛仙公者，每饮酒醉，常入人家门前陂水中卧，竟日乃出。
units.en: Ge Hong tells how Immortal Ge dozed in roadside ponds.
units.literal: The Baopuzi says: Immortal Lord Ge when drunk would lie in pond water before people’s gates all day before emerging.

units.zh: 曾从吴主别，到洌州，还遇大风，百官船多没，仙公船亦沉沦，吴主甚怅恨。
units.en: Once, after taking leave of the Wu ruler and reaching Liezhou, he was caught on the return journey in a great gale. Many officials' boats went down, the Immortal Lord's boat sank as well, and the Wu ruler was deeply distressed.
units.literal: Once bidding farewell to the Wu lord and reaching Liezhou, he met a great wind; many officials' boats sank, and the Immortal Lord's boat also went under; the Wu lord deeply regretted it.

units.zh: 明日使人钩求公船，而登高以望焉。
units.en: Next day crews dragged for wreckage from the heights.
units.literal: Next day men grappled for the boat while watchers climbed high to scan.

units.zh: 久之，见公步从水上来，衣履不沾，而有酒色。
units.en: He walked ashore dry and tipsy.
units.literal: After long delay they saw him walking from the water—clothes dry—with wine-flushed face.

units.zh: 既见而言曰：“臣昨侍从而伍子胥见请，暂过设酒，忽忽不得，即委之。”
units.en: He blamed a banquet with Wu Zixu’s ghost for his delay.
units.literal: Seeing him he said: “Yesterday my attendant Wu Zixu invited me—I stopped for wine—could not linger—had to leave.”

units.zh: 又有姚光者，有火术。
units.en: Yao Guang commanded flame.
units.literal: Also Yao Guang practiced fire arts.

units.zh: 吴主身临试之，积荻数千束，使光坐其上，又以数千束荻裹之，因猛风而燔之。
units.en: Sun Quan piled reeds, seated Yao Guang, torched the heap.
units.literal: The Wu lord personally tested—stacked thousands of reed bundles—had Guang sit atop—wrapped thousands more—blazed them with fierce wind.

units.zh: 荻了尽，谓光当以化为烬，而光端坐灰中，振衣而起，把一卷书。
units.en: Ash fell away—Yao Guang stood untouched with a book.
units.literal: When reeds burned out they expected Guang reduced to ash—yet Guang sat upright in ashes—shook his robes and rose—holding a scroll.

units.zh: 吴主取其书视之，不能解也。
units.en: Sun Quan could not read the script.
units.literal: The Wu lord took the book—could not decipher it.

units.zh: 又曰：吴景帝有疾，求觋视者，得一人。
units.en: Emperor Jing of Wu sought healers—found a medium.
units.literal: Also: Wu Jingdi fell ill—sought a spirit medium—found one.

units.zh: 景帝欲试之，乃杀鹅而埋於苑中，架小屋，施床几，以妇人屐履服物著其上，乃使觋视之。
units.en: He staged a fake tomb with goose remains and women’s gear.
units.literal: Jingdi wished to test—killed a goose buried in the garden—built a hut—bed and desk—placed woman’s shoes and garments atop—sent the medium to view.

units.zh: 告曰：“若能说此冢中鬼妇人形状者，当加赏而即信矣。”
units.en: Success meant reward—describe the ghost woman.
units.literal: Told him: “If you can describe this tomb ghost woman’s shape—you shall be rewarded and trusted.”

units.zh: 竟日尽夕无言，帝推问之急，乃曰：“实不见有鬼，但见一头白鹅立墓上，所以不即白之，疑是鬼神变化作此相，当候其真形而定。
units.en: Pressed hard, the medium finally said, “I truly saw no ghost—only a white goose standing on the tomb. I did not report at once because I suspected spirits had disguised themselves thus—I waited to determine the true form.
units.literal: All day to evening no word—the emperor pressed urgently—then said: “Truly saw no ghost—only a white goose on the tomb—did not report immediately—suspected spirit disguise—waited for true form.

units.zh: 无复移易，不知何故，不敢不以实上闻。”
units.en: There was no further change; I know not why—but I dared not report anything but the truth.”
units.literal: No further change—know not why—dare report only truth.”

units.zh: 景帝乃厚赐之。
units.en: The emperor paid him well.
units.literal: Jingdi richly rewarded.

units.zh: 然则鹅死亦有鬼也。
units.en: Pei wonders whether geese have ghosts.
units.literal: Thus even a dead goose has a ghost?

units.zh: 葛洪《神仙传》曰：仙人介象，字元则，会稽人，有诸方术。
units.en: Ge Hong’s hagiography introduces Jie Xiang of Kuaiji.
units.literal: Ge Hong’s Traditions of Immortals says: Immortal Jie Xiang, courtesy Yuanze—Kuaiji—commanded many arts.

units.zh: 吴主闻之，徵象到武昌，甚敬贵之，称为介君，为起宅，以御帐给之，赐遗前后累千金，从象学蔽形之术。
units.en: Sun Quan housed him in luxury and studied concealment.
units.literal: The Wu lord summoned him to Wuchang—honored him—styled Lord Jie—built a mansion—granted imperial curtains—gifts piled to thousand gold—studied invisibility from Xiang.

units.zh: 试还后宫，及出殿门，莫有见者。
units.en: He vanished crossing palace gates.
units.literal: Tested returning through rear palace—exiting hall gate—none saw him.

units.zh: 又使象作变化，种瓜菜百果，皆立生可食。
units.en: He sprouted melons and fruits on command.
units.literal: Also had Xiang perform transformations—plant melons vegetables hundred fruits—all sprouted instantly edible.

units.zh: 吴主共论鲙鱼何者最美，象曰：“鯔鱼为上。”
units.en: Asked about sashimi, Jie Xiang praised zi fish.
units.literal: The Wu lord debated which sliced fish excelled—Xiang said: “Zi fish ranks highest.

units.zh: 吴主曰：“论近道鱼耳，此出海中，安可得邪？”
units.en: Sun Quan called sea fish unattainable inland.
units.literal: The Wu lord said: “Speaking of nearby river fish—this comes from the sea—how obtain?”

units.zh: 象曰：“可得耳。”
units.en: Jie Xiang promised delivery.
units.literal: Xiang said: “Can obtain.”

units.zh: 乃令人於殿庭中作方埳，汲水满之，并求钩。
units.en: Servants dug a pool and fetched tackle.
units.literal: Thereupon ordered a square pit dug in the courtyard—filled with water—and sought hooks.

units.zh: 象起饵之，垂纶於埳中。
units.en: He angled in the courtyard pool.
units.literal: Xiang baited—cast line into the pit.

units.zh: 须臾，果得鯔鱼。
units.en: He landed a zi fish.
units.literal: Presently obtained zi fish.

units.zh: 吴主惊喜，问象曰：“可食不？”
units.en: Sun Quan asked if it was safe to eat.
units.literal: The Wu lord delighted—asked: “Edible?”

units.zh: 象曰：“故为陛下取以作生鲙，安敢取不可食之物！”
units.en: Jie Xiang swore it suited sashimi.
units.literal: Xiang said: “Fetched for Your Majesty as raw slices—how dare bring inedible!”

units.zh: 乃使厨下切之。
units.en: Chefs carved the fish.
units.literal: Ordered the kitchen to slice.

units.zh: 吴主曰：“闻蜀使来，得蜀姜作韲甚好，恨尔时无此。”
units.en: Sun Quan said, “I heard Shu envoys came and that Shu ginger made into pickles was excellent—I regret we did not have it then.”
units.literal: The Wu lord said: “Heard Shu envoys came and brought Shu ginger made into pickles—it was excellent; regret none then.”

units.zh: 象曰：“蜀姜岂不易得，愿差所使者，并付直。”
units.en: Jie Xiang said, “Shu ginger is not hard to obtain—I wish to send the messenger along and pay for it.”
units.literal: Xiang said: “Shu ginger is not hard to obtain—I wish to send the messenger along and pay the price.”

units.zh: 吴主指左右一人，以钱五十付之。
units.en: Sun Quan picked a runner and fifty coins.
units.literal: The Wu lord pointed to an attendant—gave fifty cash.

units.zh: 象书一符，以著青竹杖中，使行人闭目骑杖，杖止，便买姜讫，复闭目。
units.en: He charmed a bamboo rod for blind teleport shopping.
units.literal: Xiang wrote a charm—placed it in a green bamboo staff—had the traveler close eyes and ride the staff—when the staff stopped buy ginger—close eyes again.

units.zh: 此人承其言骑杖，须臾止，已至成都，不知是何处，问人，人言是蜀市中，乃买姜。
units.en: The courier opened his eyes in Chengdu’s market.
units.literal: The man obeyed—presently stopped—already at Chengdu—did not know where—asked—people said Shu market—bought ginger.

units.zh: 于时吴使张温先在蜀，既於市中相识，甚惊，便作书寄其家。
units.en: He met Zhang Wen and sent mail east.
units.literal: At that time Wu envoy Zhang Wen was in Shu—recognized him in the market—startled—wrote a letter home.

units.zh: 此人买姜毕，捉书负姜，骑杖闭目，须臾已还到吴，厨下切鲙适了。
units.en: He finished buying ginger, took the letter and carried the ginger, rode the staff with eyes closed, and in an instant was back in Wu—the kitchen had just finished slicing the fish.
units.literal: The man finished buying ginger—took letter carried ginger—rode staff eyes closed—instantly back in Wu—the kitchen had just finished slicing fish.

units.zh: 臣松之以为葛洪所记，近为惑众，其书文颇行世，故撮取数事，载之篇末也。
units.en: Pei cites Ge Hong to show wonder-tales entertained readers—not sober history.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi considers Ge Hong’s records approach deluding masses—the text circulates widely—therefore excerpt several matters at chapter end.

units.zh: 神仙之术，讵可测量，臣之臆断，以为惑众，所谓夏虫不知冷冰耳。〉
units.en: Pei dismisses miracle lore as summer worms denying winter—closing the gloss.
units.literal: Immortal arts—how measure—my opinion judges them deluding masses—the so-called summer insects knowing nothing of ice—end quote.
